8. **Structured press.** First, what the reviews of items 7a and 7b decided (27 October 2026): Ṣumur a province of its own, with the phone made to read the Levant ("Map on small screens"), and Lukka a land without a king (since revised: item 11+ gives it one leader), which item 7b began too early to build; winter dangerous for passes and the open sea alike, never closed ("Winter is dangerous, never closed"), in place of 7b's closed passes and 7a's winter cut-off of the sea; and a spy's report from a watched province carried home by road like any other ("Missions"), not seen live. Then the second press mode, with templates for every king and script envoys, as under "Two press modes"; and the clauses every letter carries in full press too, so a script reads any letter by its formulas, whoever wrote the words. Also "Recognition is earned" under The world: rank as starting data, the record of who calls whom brother and grants whom the title, a new claim becoming established in play, and the general script rule that replaces Babylonia's named rule against Assyria, with the opening positions telling model kings the same facts. Also gold sent without an inventory tablet, which saves the scribe's fee and can be checked by nobody ("The check is already in the rules"). Also characters as agents in local play: local play ("Local play on a Claude subscription" under Tech stack) runs only the kings as agents, so its characters are script, which under structured press would force its model kings onto templates. Make local play able to run the characters as agents too, chosen at setup like every other model, using the simulation kit's file characters. With characters as agents, they sleep as kings do ("Characters sleep like kings"): measure wake-ups per character and calls per season, from which item 18 sets the pool's default size ("How many characters"). Also a screen at a human seat's court for its standing answers, since humans may set them too ("Standing answers" under "Minds follow what is at stake"; answering item 6b's review, 27 October 2026).
